Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The data point to mid-2023. The fed funds rate is 5.33%, which fits after the July 2023 hike. Unemployment is 3.5%, which matches July 2023, and core CPI at 4.7% fits as well. Headline CPI at 3.3% is a bit off, since June 2023 was 3.0% and July was 3.2%, and the 10-year yield at 4.12% is also lower than I'd expect for late July.

Checking the details against each candidate month:
- **July 2023:** headline CPI was 3.2%, core CPI 4.7%, and the 10-year yield about 3.96% at month end. Fed funds had just moved to 5.33%.
- **August 2023:** headline CPI was 3.7% and core CPI 4.3%. The 10-year yield was about 4.1% at month end, but unemployment was 3.8%.

The 12-month change in fed funds of +3.00 is consistent with July 2022 at 1.68% rising to 5.33%, which gives +3.65. That is a mismatch, so I considered other timings. If fed funds were 2.33% a year earlier, the date would be August 2022 to August 2023, and the August 2022 rate was 2.33%, so the change would be +3.00. That points to August 2023.

Other August 2023 checks:
- The 3-month change in fed funds of +0.25 fits, since the rate was 5.08% in May and 5.33% in August.
- The VIX at 13.88 fits the end of August 2023.
- The 10-year yield rose 0.48 over three months, from about 3.64% in May to 4.12%, which fits.
- Reported unemployment of 3.5% could be the July value, published in early August, and the CPI figures of 3.3% headline and 4.7% core could be the July readings as known at the time. The vintage may differ slightly.
- Equity 1-month return of 0.0% fits too, since August 2023 total return was about -1.6% on the S&P.

Taken together, the snapshot fits roughly July or August 2023. The 12-month change in fed funds favors the earlier of the two as month-end July (rate 5.33 vs 1.68 gives +3.65) being wrong, so I'll go with August.
